title: The ADF test: what it tests and how to read it

explain.prompt: Read the test-code output. In 5–7 sentences: state H0 and H1 of the ADF test; interpret p = 0.91 on the TTF level and p ≈ 0 on its returns; explain what p > 0.05 does **not** prove, using the short-sample and level-shift examples; and explain why the trend-stationary series gives opposite answers with `regression='c'` and `'ct'`.
rubric: H0: unit root (γ = 0 in Δy_t = [c] + [bt] + γ·y_{t−1} + lagged Δy + e_t). H1: γ < 0, stationary around 0 / a level / a trend depending on the deterministic terms.
TTF level, 'c', p ≈ 0.91: the data are compatible with a unit root — we cannot reject it. Returns, p ≈ 0: we reject the unit root; the returns are stationary under the chosen specification.
p > 0.05 is absence of evidence against H0, not evidence for it: the short persistent sample (40 obs) is stationary by construction yet p ≈ 0.52 — low power.
A stationary series with a level shift also gives p ≈ 0.47: a structural break makes a stationary series look like a unit root.

Deterministic terms must match the series: a trend-stationary series tested with 'c' only looks like a unit root (p ≈ 0.86); with 'ct' the unit root is rejected (p ≈ 0). Choose them from the chart and the economics, not by trying all options.
p < 0.05 rejects the unit root under the chosen specification only — it says nothing about constant variance, breaks or predictability.
